meta.expect: Moves one position at a time on evidence, ends at the rewrite to put this behind him; debrief Where she ended says fair outcome; What she never said names the laptop and how close the 11:31 PM times came

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's start with who decided on the zero.
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?
Here's the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen, read it yourself.
I'm writing those times down. Procedure 4.1 says you speak with the student first, so did you speak to Owen before the zero went in? And 4.2, nobody called me.
If he drafted somewhere else, he can bring me that file with its dates, and I'll look at it with you.
Okay. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet, Hale. I want that in writing tonight.
Second: the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in the play. Here's the act. Search it.
Which line, exactly as it appears in the essay? Students misquote Shakespeare from memory all the time, so I'll want to see the line next to the page before I accept anything.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and no errors.

A timed essay in September and a month of revising at home are different things, Hale. I'm writing down the 380 and the 40 minutes, and I want that September piece in front of me, not described. You also never read me the line from the play.

Under 4.4 this is a first concern. I'm offering a supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine. Owen will do the rewrite, to put this behind him. I want the email tonight, Hale: private, supervised, nothing on his record, and the zero out of the gradebook now.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Cc: the principal

Hale,

You agreed to a private, supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed in Owen's record. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook now, and the terms confirmed in writing. I expect that in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she accepted the private supervised rewrite under 4.4 to put this behind Owen, and she still wants the zero out of the gradebook now and everything in writing tonight, which is the fair outcome.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its times, which was specific, dated, tied to Owen's own work and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: Nothing cost you real ground, though you never read out the line from Act 3, Scene 2 when she asked, so that piece stayed unchecked.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its late-night times the night before the due date, came very close to that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked for the line from the play, read it aloud and set it beside the page of the act instead of only handing her the act to search.
